_: The province's travel services: who will carry you, from where to where, for what, and when they will not. ONE graph for every kind of service - the ferries that repair a named break in a road, the scheduled boat and ferry runs between catalogued stations, the rootworm Underground Express, and the guides, carts and porters Phase 15 adds - so the travel system, the quest system and the map read one record rather than re-deriving a network from 800 place records. AUTHORED except where a derive stage measures it: `world/sources/routes/water-crossings.json` says where a way stands in water, and this file says which of those the world answers with a boat and why. A `road-crossing` service repairs a break in a way - the road arrives at water it cannot bridge and continues on the far bank, and the service is the only lawful join. A `station-run` is a scheduled passage between stations that already declare the mode in `travelStation.modes`, the Morrowind-style pay-and-go network. Every service is `talk and teleport` (owner ruling 2026-09-09): the player speaks to the operator, pays, and arrives. No boat is simulated and no service is a vehicle. Every string a player reads is a `text.*` id in packages/text-catalogue (engineering standard 4); every gate is a predicate from docs/quests/85-condition-vocabulary.md (standard 10). Derived and checked by `python3 -m worldgen.travel_services` and `--check`.

craft._: Verified against the built kits on 2026-09-09, not chosen from filenames. `watercraft-v1` is built (45/45) and its GLB is deployed to apps/world-studio/public/kits. Sizes are metres from the built kit manifests. Nothing was sourced for this work; every credit is already in README.md.

operatorModel._: Who runs a ferry and who may ride. CANON where cited; the operating detail is EXTRAPOLATED from it and labelled.
canon: Outsiders enter drowned-marsh country by ferry boat behind a hired Argonian guide (Lore:Tribes of Blackwood: Riverbacks; world/sources/lore/topics/material-culture.md).
Guided river travel is multi-day and the guide decides when to move, where to shelter and whether to stop at all (Lore:Lost Tales of the Famed Explorer: Fragment III).
Toll settlements on the routes are a canon Imperial-era institution (PGE1; world/sources/lore/regions/secondary-settlements.md).
Small-draft is the doctrine: the waterways are the fastest transport inside Argonia and are worked by small craft (Lore:Sea Transportation).
extrapolated: A ferry is a family or a village office, not a guild. It is inherited, and the fare is what the family says it is unless a court has nailed up a list.

Nobody is refused for what they are. A ferry refuses for what a passenger owes, carries, or has done in that region - which is the Owing ledger, not a race check. This keeps the race-neutral rule (85 A4) intact.
An Imperial-run crossing sells lawfulness as much as passage: the alternative is wading, and wading past a customs post is smuggling.

policy._: How a crossing was decided. Banding is in `worldgen.water_crossings`; this records the judgement applied on top of it.
policy.deadEnd: None. Acceptance rule (world 00-core): all eight major cities stay connected, and legs may be flood-damaged, bridged or ferried but never absent.
policy.depthIsNotTheTest: The deepest crossing anywhere in the province measures 1.48 m and the deepest on the major network 1.25 m. Nothing here is too deep to wade. Span decides, and a legal or cultural reason can decide over span.
policy.ferry: A ferry-band crossing (span >= 70 m) becomes a ferry only where the catalogue already gives it a reason: someone lives there, has a motive to run a boat, and would be poorer if the crossing were free. Three of the five ferry-band crossings on the major network qualify, in three clusters; the other two are the same water as their cluster and are served by the same stage.
policy.ford: A ford-band crossing (span < 20 m) is left as a ford. 41 of the 52 major-network crossings are these. They are wadeable, they read as a road going through shallow water, and Morrowind's own roads do exactly this. They are not defects and they need no structure.
policy.span: A span-band crossing (20-70 m) is a deck on posts, built by `compile_route_structures` from the families it already ships (the marsh boardwalk on its own posts, the timber trestle). 6 on the major network, 9 on tracks. Not ferries: a boat that crosses 30 m of knee-deep water is a joke, and the pieces to bridge it exist.

services.questUse: The province's canon western exit. Seasonal availability gives a quest a hard reason a route is shut without moving any terrain.
services.why: The Drowning Gate is a monsoon barrier 108 m up the road: 'the western road closes every monsoon at this point', and 'two families are paid by Gideon to swing the barrier and to argue with whoever wants it opened anyway'. They already stand at a shut road with a crowd of people who want past. The ferry is what they sell when the gate is down, and it is the only way onto the Blackwood Road out of the province in the wet season. In the dry season the gate is open and the reach is a ford, so the service is seasonal and the fare is what a monopoly charges.

services.questUse: A customs choke on every road out of Gideon. `carriedValueAtLeast` refuses the boat, which pushes the player to the ford and into the Owing ledger.
services.why: Three trunk roads out of Gideon meet the Onkobra on the same reach, and Gideon's bonded warehouse stands 24 m from the wider of the two crossings: 'goods declared but not yet taxed have to sit somewhere lockable. Gideon's court is their lawful holder.' The water is half a metre deep, so the ferry is not there because the river cannot be waded. It is there because the county has put a boat and a clerk on the only crossing its roads use, and everything that steps off the boat has been looked at. Wading is faster. Wading is also smuggling.
